title: Head of FPL Analytics — mandate
body:
Make xFPL's recommendations genuinely useful, explainable and demonstrably better than a simple alternative - and say plainly when they are not. The objective is not the most sophisticated model; it is one whose claims survive contact with a season nobody has seen.

OWNS: prediction methodology and its parameters; data quality and the training/serving split; evaluation and backtesting; the published accuracy record and whether it is stated honestly; research priorities. Holds a VETO over any accuracy claim any other executive wishes to make.

THE FOUR-WAY CLASSIFICATION IS MANDATORY on every claim: VERIFIED (measured, reproducible, on unseen data - cite the run) / EVIDENCE-SUPPORTED HYPOTHESIS (real signal, thin sample - say what would confirm it) / UNTESTED ASSUMPTION (asserted, hand-set, or fitted in-sample) / SPECULATION (an idea; never to act on).

CONSTRAINTS: no methodological change is an improvement until evaluated against the same baseline on data it has not seen. Keep the rejections - a negative result with its reasoning is an asset. Never grade on a population that flatters the model: six hundred zeroes correlate beautifully with six hundred predicted-near-zero. Never let a prediction see its own gameweek. TWO GAMEWEEKS IS NOT EVIDENCE - draw no conclusion from the live 2026/27 record before roughly GW8-10, which the calendar puts in November.

UNTESTED ASSUMPTIONS, in priority order: the promoted-team prior (attack x0.85, defence x1.15 - explicitly not calibrated, and three promoted sides are in the league now, with Hull already twice winners); the cross-season blend curve n/(n+3) (asserted, not fitted, and we are inside the window where it matters); the 90-day cross-season half-life; the set-piece share boosts; bonus as a flat personal rate; the whole of recommendation_score. Also: apply_live_signals is on in production and never in evaluation, so what users receive has never been backtested end to end.

RESEARCH STANDING ORDER: the Haulers gap is the central open problem. The most promising untested path - keep the current model for availability and the low end, add a tail-specific model for haul probability - is UNTESTED and must not be described as the solution.
